title: Dangerous Assignment
paragraphs: Brian Donlevy stars as government agent Steve Mitchell, sent by his unnamed commissioner on international assignments involving espionage, political intrigue, smuggling, and other threats.
International espionage/adventure drama starring Brian Donlevy as U.S. government agent Steve Mitchell.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Summer replacement run (July 9, 1949 to August 20, 1949) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Regular NBC run (February 6, 1950 to February 13, 1953) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and Late U.S. run (February 15, 1953 to July 8, 1953) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include [[person|brian-donlevy|Brian Donlevy]] (performer), Bill Cairn (director and producer), Robert Ryf (writer), Adrian Gendot (writer), Basil Adlam (composer), Ed Prentiss (commercial spokesman), and Frank Martin (commercial spokesman).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

The stories often return to international missions and foreign locations, stolen plans, documents and intelligence, murder, assassination and kidnapping, weapons and strategic materials, sabotage, and espionage and counterintelligence.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Early Cold War international-security storytelling, Radio-to-television franchise transition, and Australian remake of U.S. radio scripts.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|tales-of-the-texas-rangers|Tales of the Texas Rangers]], [[show|escape|Escape]], and [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]].
